title: Canadian Cyber Centre warns AI is making cyberattacks faster and easier to carry out, news reports say
date_note: The CFVR news article is dated 24 November and gives no earlier day for the warning.
geo_basis: agency: national cyber agency based in Ottawa; location not stated in the article
summary: Fort McMurray radio station CFVR's news site reports that the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security warns AI is making cyberattacks faster, more sophisticated and easier to carry out. The agency is said to be especially worried about autonomous AI systems that find weaknesses, bypass defences, deploy malware and hide evidence of intrusions. The article says attacks could target industrial control systems running energy, water and wastewater services.
plain: Canada's cyber agency warns, according to a radio station's news site, that AI makes cyberattacks faster and easier, including autonomous systems that find weaknesses and deploy malware.
exec: A radio station's news site reports the agency's warning that AI-driven attacks are getting faster and easier, and could target energy, water and wastewater control systems.

sources.name: Yam News (relays the Play 103.7 article), 25 Nov 2026

validation.note: The CFVR article is the only original; Yam News relays it. The agency's own page for this warning was not found; its October agentic-AI bulletin page was read but does not contain this warning.

review.note: Compared title, date, summary with CFVR article
